content: It seems that recent versions of Lean do not have XML directly. Has it moved somewhere?
Do you mean an inductive type for XML, or a syntax for it, or ..?
I mean there was an inductive type and a parser like for Json on Lean.Data.Xml I believe
Web searches still show this but Mathlib docs has nothing now
Oh right, the module just imports things now (or has always been like that). They are still in Lean.Data.Xml.Basic/Parser.

Thanks @𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 . But things are still puzzling me. The search https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/search.html?q=Lean.Xml.Element yields nothing. Further, I get an error if I try the following:

import Lean.Data.Xml.Basic

or alternatively 

import Lean.Data

open Lean Xml
Oh, oops, I linked to an old revision. Indeed, it was removed in lean4#12302.
Okay, so this was expelled from core lean. Was it moved to docgen? Or somewhere else (std, batteries, separate package)?
Otherwise it may be worth copying these into a separate package (I will do so if it is not being done more centrally).
It was not needed downstream so it is free for the taking
Doc-gen seems to be getting the type - not the parser - from BibtexQuery now.
In case anyone else needs it, I have copied the code to https://github.com/siddhartha-gadgil/LeanXml
